name: WEconnect Recovery
one_liner: Free recovery app for substance use with daily online peer-led meetings, routines and rewards; one-to-one peer support through some insurers.
best_for: People in recovery from alcohol or drug use who want free daily online peer meetings
People in opioid treatment whose program offers WEconnect rewards for recovery activities
People who want help keeping a daily recovery routine
not_for: Anyone in crisis or at risk of overdose: call or text 988, or 911 in an emergency
People who need medical detox or medication treatment on their own (the app supports, not replaces, treatment)
People uncomfortable with location check-ins being visible to a care team
short_description: Recovery app with free daily online peer-led meetings and routine tracking; one-to-one peer support comes through some employers, insurers or a paid plan.
long_description: WEconnect Health (formerly WEconnect Recovery) is an app for people recovering from substance use and mental health problems. The free version offers daily online support meetings led by peer specialists, including specialty meetings for women, LGBTQIA+ people, harm reduction, and family members, plus a routine planner with reminders and check-ins. Treatment programs can use it for app-based contingency management, where completing recovery activities earns gift-card rewards, and staff can see a member's activity on a dashboard. One-to-one peer support is offered to people signed up through an employer, insurer or treatment program; reviews report a self-pay premium of $40/month or $350/year. The company describes itself as a HIPAA business associate. A 2024 cohort study in Texas found that adding WEconnect contingency management to medication for opioid use disorder was linked to fewer days of opioid use and longer retention.
patient_summary: You download the WEconnect Health app, sign up with your name and phone number, and can join free online support meetings led by peer specialists throughout the day. You can also build a daily recovery routine and earn rewards for sticking to it. One-to-one peer support is offered through some employers and insurers, and reviews describe a paid plan of about $40 a month.

pricing.notes: Meetings and routines are free. One-to-one peer support is offered through employers, insurers or treatment programs; the $40/month or $350/year self-pay premium is from a 2026 review, not the vendor's site.

privacy.notes: Policy (read 2026-10-27) says WEconnect does not sell personal information, does not share it for cross-context behavioral advertising, and does not use cookies for ad profiles or cross-site tracking; all personal data can be deleted on request; acts as a HIPAA business associate.

seo.title: WEconnect Recovery: Peer Support App for Addiction
seo.meta_description: WEconnect offers peer-led virtual recovery meetings for addiction and mental health. Free app with premium coaching. 84% report improvement.

faqs.a: WEconnect is a peer support recovery app offering virtual meetings led by peer specialists, personalized recovery routines, and 1:1 coaching for people with substance use disorders and mental health challenges.
The free version includes unlimited virtual meetings, journaling, and meditation. Premium subscriptions with 1:1 peer coaching cost $40/month or $350/year, and some insurance plans cover it.
Yes, WEconnect offers specialty meetings at least once daily for specific groups including women, veterans, mothers, and LGBTQIA+ members, in addition to general themed meetings.

faqs.q: Can clinicians monitor patient progress on WEconnect?
faqs.a: Yes, WEconnect provides a HIPAA-compliant data dashboard for clinical teams to monitor patient progress and receive alerts about potential relapse risks.

clinical_trials.study: Medication for opioid use disorder with vs without WEconnect app-based contingency management, Texas

citation.authors: Marino EN, Karns-Wright T, Perez MC, Potter JS
citation.title: Smartphone App-Based Contingency Management and Opioid Use Disorder Treatment Outcomes

clinical_trials.outcome: App users reported fewer days of opioid use (8.4 vs 12.0) and stayed in treatment longer (290 vs 236 days); participants chose their group.

primary_uses: Contingency management rewards in opioid treatment
One-to-one peer support (through employer, insurer or paid plan)

availability.note: App and free meetings available in the US; one-to-one peer support mainly through employers, insurers and treatment programs.
